questions.question: Consolidating the unions into phlix-contracts requires cutting v0.3.12 and repinning both clients, which drags the 2 unreleased contracts commits into them. How do you want to scope this?

options.label: Consolidate now (Recommended)
options.description: contracts PR → tag v0.3.12 → ui + mobile PRs repin and re-export MediaType from contracts. Permanently kills the drift class (this is the 3rd divergence). Cost: both clients also pick up the Phase C metadata-sync + poster_srcset changes; contracts is types-only + a few additive helpers, so risk is low but the blast radius is wider than a type fix.

options.label: Fix in place ×3, consolidate later
options.description: Three fully independent PRs, each just correcting its own union to the 13 members. Zero coupling, trivially reviewable and revertable, no unrelated changes ride along. Leaves three copies that can drift a 4th time — I'd file the consolidation as a tracked follow-up.

options.label: Consolidate, but release contracts clean first
options.description: Cut v0.3.12 containing ONLY the MediaType/AnyMediaItem fix (branch from the v0.3.11 tag, leaving Phase C unreleased on master). Clients get the type fix with no unrelated payload. Costs an extra release branch and leaves master's history slightly forked from the release line.

  | 'music'
  | 'album'
  | 'artist'
  | 'video'
  | 'audio'
  | 'book'

/**
 * Discriminated union over the four hierarchy item shapes, narrowable on the
 * `type` discriminant. Consumers can `switch (item.type)` and let the compiler
 * enforce exhaustiveness (a default branch typed `never` flags an unhandled
 * variant).
 *
 * NOTE: this union covers the `movie`/`series`/`season`/`episode` discriminants
 * only; the broader `MediaType` also includes `audio`/`image`, which have no
 * dedicated interface yet (they surface as plain `MediaItem`). All members
 * inherit the base `MediaItem` fields, including the detail-only `user_data`.
 */
export type AnyMediaItem = Movie | Series | Season | Episode;
tool_input.new_string:
/**
 * Any item whose `type` has no dedicated interface — everything outside the
 * `movie`/`series`/`season`/`episode` video hierarchy (`track`, `music`,
 * `album`, `artist`, `video`, `audio`, `book`, `photo`, `audiobook`). These
 * surface as a plain `MediaItem` with the discriminant narrowed.
 *
 * Deriving the type via `Exclude` rather than listing the members keeps this
 * automatically correct when `MediaType` gains a member: the new member lands
 * here until it earns its own interface, so `AnyMediaItem` stays total.
 */
export interface OtherMediaItem extends MediaItem {
  type: Exclude<MediaType, 'movie' | 'series' | 'season' | 'episode'>;
}

/**
 * Discriminated union over every item shape the server can emit, narrowable on
 * the `type` discriminant. `Movie`/`Series`/`Season`/`Episode` carry the
 * hierarchy-specific fields; everything else is an `OtherMediaItem`. All members
 * inherit the base `MediaItem` fields, including the detail-only `user_data`.
 *
 * Exhaustiveness: a `switch (item.type)` that handles the four hierarchy cases
 * does NOT exhaust this union, and a `default` branch typed `never` will not
 * compile — which is the point. Real responses contain `photo`/`book`/`track`
 * rows, so a `never` default was always a lie about the runtime data; it merely
 * failed to say so while `MediaType` was missing those members. Narrow the
 * `default` branch to `OtherMediaItem` and handle it, or switch on the specific
 * discriminants you support and fall through for the rest.
 */
export type AnyMediaItem = Movie | Series | Season | Episode | OtherMediaItem;

fix(media): MediaType to full media_items.type ENUM; drop bogus `image`

`MediaType` had drifted to a stale six members and carried an `image` member
the server never emits. The real column ENUM (server migrations 001 -> 011 ->
034, `MediaItemShaper::VALID_TYPES`, and media-item.schema.json) has 13:
movie, series, season, episode, track, music, album, artist, video, audio,
book, photo, audiobook. The photo kind is named `photo`; `image` is a
scanner-side label keying the file-extension set and never reaches the wire.

Same stale list in `MediaItemShaper::VALID_TYPES` was silently relabelling
real photo/book/audiobook/track rows as "movie" in API responses
(phlix-server#527). These client-side unions are unchecked casts so nothing
failed at runtime — they were just wrong.

Also fixes `AnyMediaItem`, whose doc comment invited `switch (item.type)` with
a `never` default for exhaustiveness. That advice was unsafe: real responses
carry photo/book/track rows, so the `never` default was always a lie about the
runtime data — it just could not say so while `MediaType` omitted those
members. Rather than only documenting the hazard, the union is widened with an
`OtherMediaItem` catch-all derived via `Exclude`, so exhaustive narrowing is
genuinely sound again and a future `MediaType` member cannot silently escape.

Bumps to v0.3.12 so phlix-ui and phlix-mobile-client can repin and re-export
`MediaType` from here instead of keeping a third and fourth divergent copy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

unset GITHUB_TOKEN GH_TOKEN; gh pr create --title "fix(media): MediaType to full media_items.type ENUM; drop bogus \`image\`; widen AnyMediaItem" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

`MediaType` had drifted to a stale six members (`movie|series|season|episode|audio|image`) and carried an **`image` member the server never emits**.

The authoritative enum — server migrations 001 → 011 → 034, `MediaItemShaper::VALID_TYPES`, and `phlix-shared/schemas/media-item.schema.json` — has **13** members:

```
movie, series, season, episode, track, music, album, artist, video, audio, book, photo, audiobook
```

The photo concept is named **`photo`**. `image` is a scanner-side label keying the media scanner's file-extension set; it never reaches the wire.

## Why now

phlix-server#527 (merged) fixed the *same* stale list in `MediaItemShaper::VALID_TYPES`, where it was silently relabelling real `photo`/`book`/`audiobook`/`track` rows as `"movie"` in API responses. The client-side unions are unchecked casts, so nothing fails at runtime — they are just wrong, and they had each drifted separately in three repos.

## `AnyMediaItem`

Its doc comment explicitly invited `switch (item.type)` with a `never` default for exhaustiveness. **That advice was unsafe** — real responses carry `photo`/`book`/`track` rows, so the `never` default was always a lie about the runtime data; it merely could not say so while `MediaType` omitted those members.

Rather than only documenting the hazard, the union is widened with an `OtherMediaItem` catch-all:

```ts
export interface OtherMediaItem extends MediaItem {
  type: Exclude<MediaType, 'movie' | 'series' | 'season' | 'episode'>;
}
export type AnyMediaItem = Movie | Series | Season | Episode | OtherMediaItem;
```

Deriving via `Exclude` (rather than listing members) means a future `MediaType` member lands in `OtherMediaItem` automatically and cannot silently escape the union. Exhaustive narrowing is genuinely sound again — the `default` branch narrows to `OtherMediaItem` instead of failing to be `never`.

### Compatibility

Widening the union is technically breaking for any consumer whose `switch` asserts a `never` default. That is intentional and desirable: such code is exactly the code that was wrong about runtime data. No such consumer exists in-tree — `AnyMediaItem`'s only users are this repo's tests.

## Tests

- Exhaustiveness test updated: `default` now narrows to `OtherMediaItem`, with added `photo`/`book`/`track` cases (a photo row is precisely what server#527 was relabelling).
- New guard test asserts the union is exactly 13 members and that `image` is rejected (via `@ts-expect-error`), so this drift cannot silently recur.
- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run test:run` 52/52 pass.
- `dist/` rebuilt and committed (this repo ships prebuilt dist for github consumption).

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)

Bumped to **v0.3.12** so the two client copies can repin and re-export from here instead of maintaining divergent lists:
- `phlix-ui` — repin + re-export, plus its now-wrong type-keyed icon/link/filter spots.
- `phlix-mobile-client` — repin + re-export; its `types/contracts.ts` documents that `MediaType` consolidation was *deferred precisely because* contracts said `audio|image` where mobile said `music|photo`. This PR dissolves that blocker.

EOF

Author: Joe Huss <detain@interserver.net>
Date:   Sat Aug 1 21:34:04 2026 -0400

    fix(music)!: mediaItemId is a CHAR(36) UUID string, not a number (S123) (#26)
    
    `MusicArtist.mediaItemId` and `MusicAlbum.mediaItemId` were `number | null`
    and `MusicTrack.mediaItemId` was `number`. The column is `media_items.id`, a
    CHAR(36) UUID. It was never a number.
    
    This is the type-level half of phlix-server S121, where the identical wrong
    assumption was encoded as an `is_numeric()` test applied to a UUID. That test
    can never pass, so the field was silently `null` on the artist/album DTOs and
    silently `0` on the track DTO for the entire life of the bug. phlix-server
    corrected all three PHP DTOs to `?string`; this aligns the contract to them,
    so the PHP side stays the source of truth.
    
    `MusicTrack.mediaItemId` also becomes NULLABLE. `0` was never a real id, it
    was the coercion's fallback wearing the costume of one, which is why that
    shape was the most dangerous of the three: a caller could not tell an absent

tool_input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log -1 --format='%h %s'
chore(build): refresh dist to match src before the v0.4.0 tag (S123b)

`dist/` was last built from a src/playback.ts that still wrote
`Array<{...}>`; src has since been reformatted to `{...}[]`. Identical
types, but it means the committed dist was not the output of the
committed src.

Verified benign before committing: both sourcemaps differ ONLY in
`sourcesContent` (the embedded copy of src/playback.ts) — `mappings` is
byte-identical in each, so there is no runtime delta. dist/Music.d.ts,
which carries the actual S123 breaking change, was already correct and
is untouched here.

This lands before the v0.4.0 tag on purpose: a tag that captures a stale
dist/ ships the wrong artifact to every consumer that pins by tag, and
the staleness is invisible because the build is not run on install.

Gate: tsc --noEmit clean, vitest 77/77 in 8 files, vite build clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

"""Apply one dash_url mutation to src/playback.ts and PROVE it landed.

Usage: mutate.py <anchor-line> <inserted-line>
Inserts <inserted-line> immediately after the unique line whose stripped text
equals <anchor-line>, then prints a before/after diff of that region. Exits
non-zero if the anchor is not unique or the file is unchanged.
"""

import difflib

PATH = '/home/sites/phlix/phlix-contracts/src/playback.ts'
anchor, inserted = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

before = open(PATH).read()
lines = before.split('\n')
hits = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.strip() == anchor]
if len(hits) != 1:
    sys.exit(f'ABORT: anchor {anchor!r} matched {len(hits)} lines, need exactly 1')
idx = hits[0]
indent = lines[idx][: len(lines[idx]) - len(lines[idx].lstrip())]
lines.insert(idx + 1, indent + inserted)
after = '\n'.join(lines)

if after == before:
    sys.exit('ABORT: mutation was a NO-OP, file byte-identical')

open(PATH, 'w').write(after)

print('--- MUTATION LANDED, unified diff: ---')
sys.stdout.writelines(

        fromfile='playback.ts BEFORE', tofile='playback.ts AFTER',

)

### Changed

- 🔴 **BREAKING** — `music`: `MusicArtist.mediaItemId`, `MusicAlbum.mediaItemId`
tool_input.new_string:
## [Unreleased]

### Removed

- 🔴 **BREAKING** — `playback`: `dash_url` is gone from both
  `TranscodeStartResponse` and `TranscodeStatusResponse`. It was declared
  **required** (`dash_url: string`) on both, but the server has never sent it
  since phlix-server **S11** — real DASH is unbuilt (tracked as S56-S60), so the
  advertised `/dash/{job}/manifest.mpd` always 404'd.
  - Declaring it was strictly worse than omitting it: a consumer trusting the
    type got a compile-time guarantee of a field that is `undefined` at runtime,
    with no `strictNullChecks` warning to catch the difference.
  - Removed outright rather than relaxed to `dash_url?: string`. An optional
    member invites every consumer to keep testing for a key that is never
    emitted. When DASH actually ships it returns as a required field, in
    lockstep with the server payload.
  - The absence is pinned at the type level in `test/renditions.test.ts`
    ("declares no dash_url on either transcode shape") using the same
    `Exact<A, B>` invariant helper as `test/music.test.ts`, via
    `Exact<HasKey<T, 'dash_url'>, false>`. Because `keyof` includes optional
    members, re-adding `dash_url?: string` is just as RED as re-adding it
    required. ⚠ The killing gate is `tsc --noEmit` (`npm run typecheck`, and
    again inside `npm run build`) — vitest transpiles without type-checking and
    stays green on the mutant.
  - **Impact today: none observed.** Repo-wide greps found no reader of
    `dash_url` in `phlix-ui`, `phlix-windows-client` or `phlix-console-client`.
    `phlix-mobile-client` keeps its own local copy of these shapes plus a
    fixture that sets the key; it does not import them from here yet, so it is
    unaffected until it switches over. The clients pin `@phlix/contracts` by
    **git tag**, so this change is inert for each of them until that pin is
    deliberately bumped.

### Changed

- 🔴 **BREAKING** — `music`: `MusicArtist.mediaItemId`, `MusicAlbum.mediaItemId`

tool_input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(playback)!: remove the 404'ing dash_url from both transcode shapes (S11)

`TranscodeStartResponse.dash_url` and `TranscodeStatusResponse.dash_url` were
declared REQUIRED (`dash_url: string`), but phlix-server stopped emitting the
key in S11 (`7d171afa`, PR #536/#607): real DASH is unbuilt (tracked as
S56-S60), so the advertised `/dash/{job}/manifest.mpd` always 404'd.

Declaring it was strictly worse than omitting it — a consumer trusting the
type got a compile-time guarantee of a field that is `undefined` at runtime.

Removed outright rather than relaxed to `dash_url?: string`: an optional
member invites every consumer to keep testing for a key that is never sent.
When DASH ships it returns as a required field, in lockstep with the server.

Pinned the absence at the type level in `test/renditions.test.ts` with the
repo's existing `Exact<A, B>` invariant helper (as in `test/music.test.ts`):

    assertExact<Exact<HasKey<TranscodeStartResponse,  'dash_url'>, false>>(true)
    assertExact<Exact<HasKey<TranscodeStatusResponse, 'dash_url'>, false>>(true)

`keyof` includes optional members, so re-adding `dash_url?: string` is just as
RED as re-adding it required — which a plain assignability/fixture check does
NOT catch. Two counterweight assertions on `master_url` prove the helper can
still report `true`, so the pin is not vacuous.

tool_input.content:
/**
 * MCP (Model Context Protocol) personal-access-token vocabulary.
 *
 * The single cross-repo home for the scope strings an MCP PAT may carry and
 * for the plaintext token prefix. Authored from the hub's PHP source of truth —
 * `phlix-hub/src/Mcp/McpScopes.php` (`McpScopes::all()`, the four `const string`
 * members) and `phlix-hub/src/Mcp/McpTokenService.php` (`TOKEN_PREFIX`) — and
 * NOT derived from any client's copy.
 *
 * ## Why this lives here and not in a client (S249)
 *
 * phlix-ui previously pinned its `MCP_SCOPES` against the hub by *reading the
 * PHP file off the filesystem*, guarded by `it.runIf(existsSync(...))`. CI has
 * no `phlix-hub` checkout, so that assertion never executed and reported as
 * PASSING, while on a developer box it went red whenever the sibling tree
 * moved. Contracts is the only place both repos can depend on: the JS clients
 * already pin `@phlix/contracts` by git tag, and the hub can gate its PHP
 * constants against this file in its own CI. Neither side needs the other's
 * working tree to check itself.
 *
 * ⚠ These are the WIRE values. A consumer must compare against them exactly —
 * `'mcp:playback'` is a prefix of `'mcp:playback:control'`, so any substring /
 * `startsWith` / `includes` check silently accepts a renamed scope.
 *
 * ⚠ Scopes only ever SUBTRACT from the hub's identity+ownership gate. Holding
 * every scope in {@link MCP_SCOPES} still does not let a token reach a server
 * its user does not own. Never treat a scope as an authorization decision on
 * the client side.
 * @copyright 2026 Joe Huss <detain@interserver.net>
 */

/**
 * The closed set of MCP token scopes, keyed by the hub's constant names
 * (mirror `McpScopes::SERVERS_READ` … `McpScopes::PLAYBACK_CONTROL`).
 */
export const MCP_SCOPE = {
  /** Enumerate the media servers the token's user owns. */
  SERVERS_READ: 'mcp:servers:read',
  /** Read library / media metadata from an owned server over the relay. */
  LIBRARY_READ: 'mcp:library:read',
  /** Read playback information (stream decisions) for an owned media item. */
  PLAYBACK_READ: 'mcp:playback:read',
  /**
   * Control an ALREADY-RUNNING cast/DLNA session on an owned server: pause,
   * resume, stop, seek (hub S63). The only WRITE scope in the set, and
   * deliberately separate from {@link MCP_SCOPE.PLAYBACK_READ} — a token minted
   * so an agent can answer "what would this play as?" must not thereby be able
   * to stop somebody's film.
   */
  PLAYBACK_CONTROL: 'mcp:playback:control',
} as const;

/** One of the scopes {@link MCP_SCOPE} enumerates. */
export type McpScope = (typeof MCP_SCOPE)[keyof typeof MCP_SCOPE];

/**
 * Every MCP scope this contract version knows, in `McpScopes::all()`'s order.
 *
 * ⚠ The ORDER is part of the stored representation. `McpScopes::parse()` emits
 * scopes in this order and `mcp_tokens.scopes` stores the result, so appending
 * is safe but REORDERING rewrites what every existing row compares equal to.
 * Read-only scopes first, then writes.
 */
export const MCP_SCOPES = [
  MCP_SCOPE.SERVERS_READ,
  MCP_SCOPE.LIBRARY_READ,
  MCP_SCOPE.PLAYBACK_READ,
  MCP_SCOPE.PLAYBACK_CONTROL,
] as const;

/**
 * The prefix every minted MCP plaintext token carries
 * (`McpTokenService::TOKEN_PREFIX`).
 *
 * ⚠ Display/verification hint ONLY. A string starting with this is not an
 * authenticated token; only the hub, which holds the SHA-256 hashes, can say
 * that. Never gate anything on it client-side.
 */
export const MCP_TOKEN_PREFIX = 'phlix-mcp-';

## [0.4.2] - 2026-08-07

### Added

- `mcp`: **new module** — the MCP personal-access-token vocabulary, so the hub
  and the JS clients can pin against a shared third party instead of against
  each other's working trees. Exports `MCP_SCOPE` (the four constants, keyed by
  the hub's PHP constant names), `MCP_SCOPES` (the full list in
  `McpScopes::all()` order), the `McpScope` union, and `MCP_TOKEN_PREFIX`.
  - Authored **from** `phlix-hub/src/Mcp/McpScopes.php` and
    `McpTokenService.php`, which remain the source of truth. It is deliberately
    NOT generated from any client's copy — a vocabulary derived from its own
    consumer can never disagree with that consumer.
  - Includes **`mcp:playback:control`** (hub S63), the write scope, which
    phlix-ui's local copy did not carry.
  - **Why (phlix-ui S249):** phlix-ui pinned its `MCP_SCOPES` by reading the
    hub's PHP file off the filesystem under
    `it.runIf(existsSync(<sibling phlix-hub path>))`. CI has no `phlix-hub`
    checkout, so the assertion never ran and reported as **passing** — while on
    a developer box it went red whenever the sibling tree moved. Measured on
    phlix-ui `6efe3588`: with the sibling present the suite is `1 failed |
    5101 passed | 10 skipped`; with it absent (CI's situation, same commit,
    same live drift) it is `259 files passed, 5100 passed | 12 skipped` — fully
    green.
  - ⚠ Consumers must compare the whole list **exactly and in order**.
    `'mcp:playback'` is a prefix of `'mcp:playback:control'`, so any
    `includes` / `startsWith` check silently accepts a rename. The order is
    part of the stored representation (`McpScopes::parse()` emits in this order
    into `mcp_tokens.scopes`), so appending is safe and reordering is not.
  - ⚠ Anti-vacuity: an equality check against an export that resolves to
    `undefined` or `[]` passes trivially. Assert a floor on the length;
    `test/mcp.test.ts` pins `MCP_SCOPES.length >= 4`.

## [0.4.2] - 2026-08-07

### Added

- `mcp`: **new module** — the MCP personal-access-token vocabulary, so the hub
  and the JS clients can pin against a shared third party instead of against
  each other's working trees. Exports `MCP_SCOPE` (the four constants, keyed by
  the hub's PHP constant names), `MCP_SCOPES` (the full list in
  `McpScopes::all()` order), the `McpScope` union, and `MCP_TOKEN_PREFIX`.
  - Authored **from** `phlix-hub/src/Mcp/McpScopes.php` and
    `McpTokenService.php`, which remain the source of truth. It is deliberately
    NOT generated from any client's copy — a vocabulary derived from its own
    consumer can never disagree with that consumer.

tool_input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(mcp): vendor the MCP scope vocabulary so both repos can pin against it (S249)

phlix-ui pinned its MCP_SCOPES against phlix-hub by reading McpScopes.php off
the filesystem, guarded by it.runIf(existsSync(<sibling phlix-hub path>)).
phlix-ui's CI has no phlix-hub checkout, so that assertion never executed and
reported as PASSING; on a dev box it did the opposite wrong thing and went red
whenever the sibling tree moved.

Measured on phlix-ui 6efe3588, same commit, same live drift:
  sibling present -> 1 failed | 5101 passed | 10 skipped
  sibling absent  -> 259 files passed, 5100 passed | 12 skipped  (fully green)

Contracts is the only location both repos can depend on, and the JS clients
already pin @phlix/contracts by git tag. src/mcp.ts is authored FROM the hub's
PHP (McpScopes::all() and McpTokenService::TOKEN_PREFIX), never generated from
a client's copy -- a vocabulary derived from its own consumer can never
disagree with that consumer.

Includes mcp:playback:control (hub S63), the write scope, which phlix-ui's
local copy did not carry.

test/mcp.test.ts restates the wire values independently rather than reading
them back off src/mcp.ts, compares the whole list in order (never a substring
or membership check -- 'mcp:playback' is a prefix of 'mcp:playback:control'),
and pins an anti-vacuity floor of >= 4 members so an empty or undefined export
cannot pass an equality check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && git rev-parse HEAD

 *
 * Two of these are cross-repo pins rather than unit tests: the scope vocabulary
 * and the token prefix are the two places where a silent divergence would
 * produce a form that offers a value the server rejects, or a UI that describes
 * a credential shape that no longer exists.
 *
 * ## S249 — those two pins used to be unrunnable in CI
 *
 * As S243 shipped them they read `phlix-hub`'s PHP source off the filesystem,
 * guarded by `it.runIf(existsSync(<sibling phlix-hub path>))`. phlix-ui's CI has
 * no `phlix-hub` checkout, so the guard was always false: the assertions never
 * executed and the file reported as **passing** — measured on `6efe3588` as
 * `6 passed | 2 skipped` while a real 4-vs-3 scope drift sat in the tree. On a
 * developer box the same guard did the opposite wrong thing and went **red**
 * whenever a phlix-hub writer moved that tree, on branches touching zero MCP
 * files.
 *
 * They now pin against **`@phlix/contracts`**, an ordinary `dependencies` entry
 * resolved from `node_modules` on every machine including CI. There is no
 * filesystem probe, no `runIf`, and no try/catch around the import — a missing
 * or broken contracts package is a hard import error, not a skip. A phlix-hub
 * working tree, dirty or absent, cannot influence this file's result at all.
 *
 * ⚠ Do NOT "simplify" `MCP_SCOPES` in `./mcp-tokens` into a re-export of the

 * `McpScopes::all()` equals this same contracts vocabulary. Until that ships,
 * what is verified here is that **phlix-ui agrees with contracts** — not that
 * contracts still agrees with the hub.

# S249 — a cross-repo pin guarded by `it.runIf(existsSync(...))` never ran in CI

**Date:** 2026-08-07
**Repos written:** `phlix-contracts`, `phlix-ui` (sole writer in both)
**Repos read only:** `phlix-hub` (live writer — nothing written)
**Option built:** (a) — vendor the scope vocabulary into `@phlix/contracts` and pin both sides against it.
**Nothing pushed.** Branches, SHAs and the tag are local; the orchestrator pushes.

---

## 1. The defect, measured

`phlix-ui/src/api/mcp-tokens.test.ts:35` computed `HUB = <repo>/../../phlix-hub` and guarded two
cross-repo pins with `it.runIf(existsSync(...))`.

The measurement below is the load-bearing one, because it is the same commit (`6efe3588`) and the
same live drift, differing **only** in whether a sibling `phlix-hub` directory exists. I produced
the second row with a `git worktree` of `origin/master` placed under a parent with no `phlix-hub`
sibling — CI's exact situation — with `node_modules` symlinked in.

| tree | full `npx vitest run` |
|---|---|
| dev box (sibling `phlix-hub` present) | `Test Files 1 failed \| 258 passed (259)` · `Tests 1 failed \| 5101 passed \| 10 skipped (5112)` |
| **no sibling `phlix-hub` (= CI)** | **`Test Files 259 passed (259)`** · `Tests 5100 passed \| **12 skipped** (5112)` |

**CI was fully green over a real, live divergence.** The 2 extra skips *are* the pin. Narrowed to the
file:

```
$ npx vitest run src/api/mcp-tokens.test.ts     # in the no-sibling tree, BEFORE the fix
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed | 2 skipped (8)
```

The divergence it failed to catch: hub's `McpScopes::all()` declares **four** scopes (S63 added
`mcp:playback:control`); phlix-ui's `MCP_SCOPES` declared **three**.

### CI skip count, before and after (the AC asks for this explicitly)

| | phlix-ui suite | of which `mcp-tokens.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| **before, in CI** | **12 skipped** | 2 |
| **after, in CI** | **10 skipped** | **0** |

The residual 10 are two `describe.runIf(process.env.PHLIX_NETWORK_TESTS === '1')` blocks in
`src/pages/hubHelpLinks.test.ts:112` and `src/pages/admin/helpLinks.test.ts:146` — opt-in
outbound-network link checks, a deliberate and unrelated pattern. Untouched, and now the **only**
skips in the suite. The dev box and CI now report the same 10, so the two surfaces no longer
disagree about what ran.

---

## 2. Why (a), not (b) or (c)

- **(c) alone** is forbidden by the AC — it converts a silent skip into a loud skip without ever
  checking the contract.
- **(b), a fixture committed into phlix-ui**, cannot close the loop: only a phlix-ui writer would
  ever regenerate it and **hub's CI cannot see it**, so hub drifting away stays exactly as
  undetected as today.
- **(a)** puts the vocabulary somewhere both repos can reach. The JS clients already pin
  `@phlix/contracts` by git tag, so it is the house pattern.

**The vocabulary was authored FROM `phlix-hub/src/Mcp/McpScopes.php`**, not generated from
phlix-ui's `MCP_SCOPES`. A check derived from its subject self-adjusts; had I generated it from the
client, the two could never disagree. For the same reason phlix-ui's `MCP_SCOPES` is left as an
**independently authored literal** rather than being simplified into a re-export — a warning to
that effect is in the docblock of both the constant and the test.

---

## 3. What shipped

### `phlix-contracts` — branch `s249-mcp-scope-vocabulary`, commit `f07471e`, tag `v0.4.2`

- **`src/mcp.ts`** (new, exported from `src/index.ts`). Follows the repo's existing
  `SERVER_STATUS` / `JWT_ISS` shape — a `as const` object plus a derived union — rather than a new
  invented shape:
  - `MCP_SCOPE` — the four constants, keyed by the hub's PHP constant names;
  - `MCP_SCOPES` — the full list in `McpScopes::all()` order;
  - `McpScope` — the union;
  - `MCP_TOKEN_PREFIX` — `'phlix-mcp-'`, from `McpTokenService::TOKEN_PREFIX`.
- **`test/mcp.test.ts`** (new, 9 tests). Restates the wire values **independently** rather than
  reading them back off `src/mcp.ts`. Ordered whole-list comparison, a set comparison, a duplicate
  check, and a `>= 4` floor.
- **`dist/mcp-scopes.json`** (new, generated) + **`scripts/emit-mcp-scopes.mjs`**, wired into
  `npm run build`. **This exists because the hub cannot use the npm route**: `phlix-hub` has no
  `package.json`, and its `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no `setup-node` and no `npm ci`. It can
  `json_decode()` a file. Generated from the built bundle, never hand-maintained, and the script
  **refuses to emit an empty array**. `test/mcp.test.ts` asserts the committed artifact still equals
  `MCP_SCOPES`, so a stale file is a red rather than a wrong vocabulary the hub gates against.
- `eslint.config.js` — a `scripts/**/*.mjs` override declaring `console`/`process`, inline rather
  than adding the `globals` dependency.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `## [0.4.2] - 2026-08-07` + compare link; `package.json` `0.4.0 → 0.4.2`.
  Patch bump follows the house convention — every prior "Added" section (0.3.1 … 0.3.11) is a patch.

### `phlix-ui` — branch `s249-mcp-scope-contract-pin`, commit `8cf77d6f`

Branched from `origin/master` = **`6efe3588`** (the post-#321 master; not from PR #321's branch).
Because I branched *after* the merge rather than rebasing over it, there was **no `dist/` conflict
to resolve** — the rebuild touched only `McpTokensPage-*` chunks, `dist/api/mcp-tokens.d.ts` and
the two entry bundles. `IntegrationsPage-o5frGf0R.js` from master is untouched and still present.

- `package.json` / `package-lock.json` — `@phlix/contracts` `v0.3.12 → v0.4.2`
  (lock `resolved` → `f07471eb7ae23bfe77a4913b4417e2858da2ef2a`).
- `src/api/mcp-tokens.test.ts` — both pins rewritten against the contracts export. **No
  `existsSync`, no `runIf`, no try/catch around the import.**
- `src/api/mcp-tokens.ts` — `mcp:playback:control` added, with display copy (see §5).
- `src/pages/McpTokensPage.test.ts` — the omitted-`available_scopes` fallback test now compares
  against `MCP_SCOPES` with a `>= 4` box-count floor. Its `SCOPES` server mock deliberately stays at
  **3** members, narrower than the build's vocabulary, so "the checkboxes come from the server"
  remains a real assertion.
- `dist/` rebuilt and committed (a `src/` change — the other case in the brief did not apply).

**⚠ `npm install` cannot run in phlix-ui until `v0.4.2` is pushed.** The tag does not exist on
GitHub yet. I hand-edited `package-lock.json` to exactly what npm writes for a git dep (version +
`resolved` at the commit SHA) and materialized `node_modules/@phlix/contracts` by copying the
**committed** `dist/` and `package.json`. That is faithful — contracts commits `dist/` and has no
`prepare` script, so npm installs the checked-in build verbatim. Verified byte-identical:

```
31743f27fd1bc1823d3235c2b547a394  node_modules/@phlix/contracts/dist/phlix-contracts.js
31743f27fd1bc1823d3235c2b547a394  phlix-contracts/dist/phlix-contracts.js
8c92c0703eae8a429c509ff16e0d185d  node_modules/@phlix/contracts/dist/mcp-scopes.json
8c92c0703eae8a429c509ff16e0d185d  phlix-contracts/dist/mcp-scopes.json
```

After the push, `npm install` in phlix-ui should be a no-op; if it is not, the lock edit was wrong
and that is the thing to check first.

---

## 4. Gates (real exit codes, not text)

### phlix-contracts (`lint`, `typecheck`, `build`, `test:run` — the four its CI runs)

```
LINT EXIT=0
TYPECHECK EXIT=0
BUILD EXIT=0          [emit-mcp-scopes] wrote dist/mcp-scopes.json (4 scopes)
TEST EXIT=0           Test Files  9 passed (9)
                           Tests  87 passed (87)
```

Arithmetic: baseline **78** + `test/mcp.test.ts` **9** = **87**. Working tree is clean after
`npm run build`, so the committed `dist/` reproduces byte-for-byte.

> ⚠ The first lint run **failed** (`'console' is not defined` in the new `.mjs`) while my shell
> printed `lint_exit=0` — I had captured `$?` after an intervening `echo`. Every figure above is
> from a re-run that captures the exit code of the command itself. Flagging it because
> `feedback_phpcs_exit_code_lies` is the same failure mode in a different toolchain.

### phlix-ui

```
VITEST EXIT=0     Test Files  259 passed (259)
                       Tests  5104 passed | 10 skipped (5114)
ESLINT EXIT=0
VUE-TSC EXIT=0
DIST:CHECK EXIT=0  ✔ committed dist/ matches source (808 tracked files, 8 published entry points, 5/5 checks ran)
```

Arithmetic, from the dev-box baseline `1 failed | 5101 passed | 10 skipped (5112)`:

| | tests |
|---|---|
| baseline passing | 5101 |
| baseline failing, now fixed | +1 |
| new in `mcp-tokens.test.ts` (8 → 10) | +2 |
| **new passing total** | **5104** |
| skipped (unchanged; both were the network-gated describes) | 10 |
| **total** | **5114** |

`dist:check` states its own corpus size (808 files, 5/5 checks ran), so it is not a gate that
inspected zero files.

---

## 5. The live `mcp:playback:control` drift — decision and reasoning

**Decided: add it to phlix-ui's `MCP_SCOPES`, with display copy.** Not reflexively to green a test.

1. `MCP_SCOPES`' own docblock defines it as mirroring `McpScopes::all()`. It is the vocabulary, not
   a UI feature-flag list.
2. **The UI already surfaces this scope, badly.** `McpScopes::all()` returns `PLAYBACK_CONTROL`
   *unconditionally* — the operator flag gates whether `PlaybackControlTool` is *registered*, not
   whether the scope is offered — so `McpTokenController::index()` already puts it in
   `available_scopes`. `McpTokensPage.vue:404` iterates `availableScopes`, `:413` renders
   `scopeLabel(scope)` which falls back to the raw wire string, and `:415` hides the description
   when empty. So against any current hub the create form **already** shows a checkbox reading
   `mcp:playback:control` with no explanation — and `:186` seeds the selection from the whole
   vocabulary, so it is **checked by default**. A default-on WRITE scope that can stop somebody
   else's film was being offered unlabelled. Adding the copy fixes that.
3. Without it, the *fallback* path (list response omits `available_scopes`) would offer a narrower
   vocabulary than the hub accepts, and a user could not mint a control token at all.

The copy names it as the write scope: label *"Control playback already in progress (write)"*;
description *"Pause, resume, stop or seek a cast session already running on an owned server. The
only scope here that can change anything — it cannot start playback, but it can stop somebody
else's."*

---

## 6. Mutation proof

Committed first (`8cf77d6f`), then mutated. Restored by **file copy** and verified with `md5sum` —
never `git checkout --`. Baseline `src/api/mcp-tokens.ts` = `a0176eef756fbc9b533500a1221bc406`;
baseline `node_modules/@phlix/contracts/dist/phlix-contracts.js` =
`31743f27fd1bc1823d3235c2b547a394`. Both restored to those hashes, working tree clean.

Five mutants, varying the **shape** of the defect rather than repeating one:

| # | mutation | named tests that went RED | control that stayed GREEN |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `mcp:playback:control` → `mcp:playback:contro**ls**` (a **superstring** — an `.includes()`/`startsWith` check would PASS this) | `MCP_SCOPES equals the contracts vocabulary, in order` · `… as a set, ignoring order` · `every known scope has display copy` | 7 others |
| 2 | **reorder** — swap `library:read` and `playback:read` | `MCP_SCOPES equals the contracts vocabulary, in order` **only** | the set-comparison test stayed green — proving the two assertions test genuinely different things |
| 3 | **deletion** of `mcp:playback:control` (i.e. restoring the exact pre-S249 live drift) | `… in order` · `… as a set` · `McpTokensPage — … falls back to this build s vocabulary when the hub omits available_scopes` | 34 others |
| 4 | contracts' `MCP_SCOPES` emptied in `node_modules` (stale pin / bad resolution → `[]`) | `the contracts vocabulary is non-vacuous` · `… in order` · `… as a set` | 7 others |
| 5 | **both** sides emptied | **`the contracts vocabulary is non-vacuous` — and ONLY that one** | the two equality tests **passed** (`9 passed`) |

**Mutant 5 is the anti-vacuity proof.** With both vocabularies empty, the equality assertions go
green — exactly the silent pass a floor exists to prevent — and only the floor reds. The floor is
load-bearing, not decoration.

**The floors, stated:** `CONTRACT_MCP_SCOPES.length >= 4` and a non-empty `CONTRACT_MCP_TOKEN_PREFIX`
in `mcp-tokens.test.ts`; `MCP_SCOPES.length >= 4` in contracts' `test/mcp.test.ts`; `>= 4` rendered
checkboxes in `McpTokensPage.test.ts`. Four is the vocabulary as of hub S63; dropping below it must
be a deliberate edit.

### Mutant 3 replanted with NO phlix-hub on disk — the AC's core demand

Run inside the no-sibling worktree, `ls ../phlix-hub` → *No such file or directory*:

```
=== UNMUTATED ===        Test Files  1 passed (1)      Tests  10 passed (10)    [was: 6 passed | 2 skipped]
=== MUTANT 3 ===
 FAIL  src/api/mcp-tokens.test.ts > … > MCP_SCOPES equals the contracts vocabulary, in order

 FAIL  src/pages/McpTokensPage.test.ts > … > falls back to this build s vocabulary when the hub omits available_scopes
 Test Files  2 failed (2)          Tests  3 failed | 34 passed (37)
```

The divergence CI previously reported as passing now reds three named tests **with no phlix-hub
checkout anywhere**.

---

## 7. "A dirty hub tree can no longer red phlix-ui" — why impossible, not merely unlikely

Structural, not probabilistic: **`mcp-tokens.test.ts` no longer performs any filesystem access at
all.** The `node:fs`, `node:path` and `node:url` imports and the `HUB` path constant are deleted;
the only new import is `@phlix/contracts`, resolved from `node_modules`.

- `grep -rn "runIf\|existsSync\|readFileSync" src/api/mcp-tokens.test.ts` → matches only in prose
  inside the docblock that explains the old bug.
- Repo-wide `grep` for sibling-repo path construction across `src/**/*.{ts,vue}` → every hit is a
  comment or a test fixture string; no path is built.
- The remaining `node:fs` readers in the suite (`LibraryPage.test.ts`, `themeTokens.test.ts`, the
  dist gates, …) all read files **inside phlix-ui**.

Observed live: mid-session the hub writer moved `phlix-hub` from `cdda377` (dirty, 190+ modified
paths) to `b85e9f2` and then `6568835` (clean). The phlix-ui suite reported `5104 passed |
10 skipped` throughout, unchanged.

A no-filesystem-read cannot be influenced by a filesystem state.

---

## 8. ⚠ WHAT IS **NOT** VERIFIED UNTIL THE HUB COMPANION LANDS

S249's AC is **not fully met by this half.** Stating it plainly rather than claiming otherwise:

| direction | status |
|---|---|
| phlix-ui drifting away from contracts | **closed** — reds in CI, proved by mutation with no hub checkout |
| a dirty/absent phlix-hub tree reddening or greening phlix-ui | **closed** — no filesystem read remains |
| contracts drifting away from its own `dist/mcp-scopes.json` | **closed** — contracts CI |
| **phlix-hub drifting away from contracts** | ❌ **STILL UNDETECTED** |

Concretely: a hub writer who adds `MCP_SCOPES[4]` to `McpScopes::all()` tomorrow gets **green CI in
every repo**. phlix-ui and contracts will agree with each other perfectly while both are wrong about
the server. That is the same class of bug as the original — narrower, since the hub is the source of
truth and downstream now agrees internally, but it is not closed. The reverse direction (hub
*removes* a scope) is likewise silent.

There is also a **snapshot-freshness** limit worth naming: contracts' vocabulary was transcribed
from hub `McpScopes.php` and re-verified against hub HEAD `6568835` at the end of this session
(4 scopes, prefix `phlix-mcp-`). Nothing re-checks that automatically. **§9 is the whole closure.**

public function testScopeVocabularyMatchesTheContractsPackage(): void
{

    self::assertFileExists($path, 'the vendored @phlix/contracts vocabulary is missing');

    /** @var array{scopes: list<string>, tokenPrefix: string} $contract */
    $contract = json_decode((string) file_get_contents($path), true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

    // ---- ANTI-VACUITY, BEFORE any comparison ----
    // Without this, a truncated / empty / wrong-keyed fixture makes every
    // assertion below compare [] with [] and pass.
    self::assertIsArray($contract['scopes'] ?? null);
    self::assertGreaterThanOrEqual(4, count($contract['scopes']), 'FLOOR: 4 scopes as of S63');
    self::assertIsString($contract['tokenPrefix'] ?? null);
    self::assertNotSame('', $contract['tokenPrefix']);
    self::assertGreaterThanOrEqual(4, count(McpScopes::all()), 'FLOOR: McpScopes::all()');

    // ---- EXACT, ORDERED, WHOLE-LIST. assertSame, never assertEquals; never

    // 'mcp:playback:control', so a substring check passes a rename. Order is
    // asserted because McpScopes::parse() emits in all() order into the
    // mcp_tokens.scopes column. ----

        McpScopes::all(),

        . 'Fix the CONTRACT first: add the scope to phlix-contracts src/mcp.ts, npm run build, '
        . 'tag, then re-vendor dist/mcp-scopes.json here. Do NOT edit the fixture alone.'
    );

`user_data` is `null` when the request is unauthenticated; when authenticated
with no stored row it defaults to `{ "favorite": false, "rating": null, "like_level": 0 }`.

- `level` (`int -2..2`, **required**) — the signed thumbs axis: `-2` = strongly
  dislike, `-1` = dislike, `0` = not set, `1` = like, `2` = love. The `level`
  field is required (there is no "clear" / null branch — set `0` to unset).

`{"error": "level must be an integer between -2 and 2"}`; an integer outside
`-2..2` passes that guard and is rejected by the repository with
`{"error": "like_level must be between -2 and 2 (inclusive), got 3"}`

## TL;DR

Phlix Hub ships hub-to-hub **federation**, and it runs unconditionally — there is no enable/disable flag. Federation uses a **master/leaf** model: one hub is designated the master and other hubs join it as leaves. Once peered, hubs can share libraries across the trust boundary, relay leaf servers through the master, and delegate admin access. Federation is managed from the **Federation page** (`/app/federation`) and the `/api/v1/me/federation/*` REST API; peers are added **manually** (there is no automatic discovery). The one real auth limitation: there is **no cross-hub end-user single-sign-on** — a user account does not span hubs, and each hub issues its own user sessions. A single Phlix Hub instance comfortably handles ~5000 users and ~200 servers on its own, so federation is for genuinely multi-hub deployments rather than capacity overflow.

```text
# Federation REST API (live; gated by admin auth)
GET    /api/v1/me/federation/hub-config
PUT    /api/v1/me/federation/hub-config
GET    /api/v1/me/federation/peers
POST   /api/v1/me/federation/peers
DELETE /api/v1/me/federation/peers/{id}
PUT    /api/v1/me/federation/peers/{id}/relay
PUT    /api/v1/me/federation/peers/{id}/admin-delegation
```

> **Note:** The endpoints above are real and served by `FederationController`, gated behind admin authentication. See [Federation REST API](#federation-rest-api) for the complete route list.

---

### Master and leaf hubs

Federation uses a **master/leaf** topology (`federation_hubs.role` is an `ENUM('master','leaf')`):

|---|---|
| **Master hub** | The designated authority hub. Other hubs connect to it as leaves. Exactly one master per federation. |
| **Leaf hub** | A hub that connects to the master. A leaf can share librari

Federation is managed from the **Federation page** (`/app/federation`) and the `/api/v1/me/federation/*` REST API; peers are added **manually** (there is no automatic discovery). The one real auth limitation: there is **no cross-hub end-user single-sign-on** — a user account does not span hubs, and each hub issues its own user sessions. A single Phlix Hub instance comfortably handles ~5000 users and ~200 servers on its own, so federation is for genuinely multi-hub deployments rather than capacity overflow.

GET    /api/v1/me/federation/peers
POST   /api/v1/me/federation/peers

PUT    /api/v1/me/federation/peers/{id}/relay
PUT    /api/v1/me/federation/peers/{id}/admin-delegation

### Hub-to-hub transport

Leaf hubs connect to the master over a persistent **WebSocket** tunnel served by `FederationWorker` on **port 8805**. The inbound path is `/relay/federation/{hub_id}`, and the incoming `hub_id` is validated against the `federation_peers` table before the connection is accepted.   "scopes": ["mcp:servers:read", "mcp:library:read"],
  "expires_at": 1767225600
}
```

`expires_at` is an absolute Unix timestamp in seconds.

Notes on the mint body:

- Unknown scope values are **dropped**, not rejected. A list with nothing known
  left in it is a `400` (`mcp_token.no_valid_scopes`) rather than a token that
  authenticates but authorises nothing.
- **Omitting `scopes` entirely grants every scope** the hub offers. Send the key
  explicitly if you want a narrow token.
- Revoking an unknown id, an already-revoked token, or somebody else's token all
  return the same `404` (`mcp_token.not_found`) — they are deliberately
  indistinguishable so the endpoint cannot be used to probe for other users'
  token ids.

tool_input.old_string:
- **Omitting `scopes` entirely grants every scope** the hub offers. Send the key
  explicitly if you want a narrow token.
tool_input.new_string:
- **Any `scopes` value that is not a JSON array or object grants every scope**
  the hub offers, including the write scope `mcp:playback:control`. The check is
  `is_array($rawScopes)` in `McpTokenController::create()`, so omitting the key,
  sending `null`, a bare string, a number or a boolean all fall through to "all
  scopes" — `"scopes": "mcp:library:read"` asks for one scope and gets four.
  Only an array (or a JSON object, which decodes to a PHP array) is filtered
  against the known list. Note the asymmetry with the bullet above: a typo
  *inside* an array fails **closed** with a `400`, but a wrong *type* for the
  array itself fails **open**. Always send `"scopes": [ ... ]`.

  Any authenticated hub user can mint such a token — `POST /api/v1/me/mcp-tokens`
  is gated by `AuthMiddleware` alone, not admin-only. The hub's own token UI
  always sends an array, so the fail-open path is reachable only from a direct
  API call. An over-broad token is still bounded by ownership: scope is the
  second gate, and the first is that the account must already own the server.

post:
      summary: Add an extra catalog source
      description: |
        Adds an operator-supplied catalog URL to the source list. The URL must
        use an `http://` or `https://` scheme (catalogs are network documents);
        anything else is rejected with `plugin.catalog.url.invalid`. A missing
        or empty `url` yields `plugin.catalog.url.required`. The added source is
        persisted as a `plugins.catalog.sources` override in `server_settings`.

        Adding a URL that duplicates the default or an existing source is a
        no-op (it still returns `200` with the unchanged list).
      operationId: addPluginCatalogSource
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/CatalogSourceRequest'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: The full source list after the add (default first).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/CatalogSourceList'
        '400':
          description: Missing (`plugin.catalog.url.required`) or non-http(s) (`plugin.catalog.url.invalid`) URL.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorWithFields'
        '401':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'
        '403':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Forbidden'
    delete:
      summary: Remove an extra catalog source
      description: |
        Removes an operator-added catalog source. The **default source cannot
        be removed** — passing it is a no-op that returns the unchanged list.

A parent-less item — `movie`, `video`, `photo`, `book`, `audiobook` — whose file
was **moved without being renamed** is matched by a path-independent canonical key.
The scan records the new location and the prune in the same job **re-points the
existing row at it instead of deleting it**, so the item keeps its UUID, its
`user_item_data` (favorite, rating, like level, watched) and its resume position.
Episodes were never affected.

name is a different canonical key), and the standalone `prune` job, which does not
scan and so has no candidate to adopt. Full detail:
[Moving a file](../admin/library-management#moving-a-file).

prunes — the stale row survives every scan and keeps shadowing the file at its new
path. Only a rescan clears it, and clearing it is the data loss.

avoid the loss: a different name is a different canonical key, so the file is
inserted as a new row and the old row is pruned — a new UUID and lost watch state

`bin/phlix library:scan --rescan`) go through the same scanner, so neither

catalogue, it looks the file up by path (a miss, since the path changed) and

touched.

**Since:** 0.18.0

Guide for updating an existing Phlix installation to a newer version. Read the [Known breaking-change patterns](#known-breaking-change-patterns) section before every upgrade.

---

## TL;DR

```bash
# 1. Back up
sudo -u phlix cp /etc/phlix/env /var/phlix/backups/env-$(date +%Y%m%d)

# 2. Pull the new version (or use the same method as your original install)
cd /opt/phlix-server
sudo -u phlix git pull

# 3. Install dependencies
sudo -u phlix composer install --no-dev

# 4. Run database migrations
sudo -u phlix php scrip

unaffected. Restore the media to its **original paths** before rescanning; if you

workaround today. Tracked as **S158**.

## Playback fails / transcoding errors

### 1. Check the transcode log

Every transcode job writes a log to `.logs/transcode/<job-id>.log`. Find the job ID from `media.log` or `streaming.log`:

```bash
# Watch media channel for transcode job IDs
tail -f .logs/media.log | grep -i "transcode\|job"

# Read a specific transcode log
cat .logs/transcode/abc123def.log
```

### 2. Verify FFmpeg is installed and accessible

```bash
ffmpeg -version
ffprobe -version
```

If FFmpeg is not found or the version is very old, reinstall:

```bash
# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install ffmpeg

# Or use the jellyfin-ffmpeg PPA for a more up-to-date build
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:jonathonf/ffmpeg-4
sudo apt update && sudo apt install ffmpeg
```

### 3. Check hardware acceleration

```bash
# NVIDIA NVENC
ffmpeg -hide_banner -encoders 2>&1 | grep nvenc

# Intel VAAPI
vainfo

# Intel Quick Sync
ffmpeg -hide_banner -encoders 2>&1 | g

## Library & Media

### Which file formats does Phlix play directly, and which need transcoding?

Phlix uses FFmpeg for playback. Direct-play (no transcoding) depends on your client's codec support, but common direct-play formats include H.264/AAC in MP4/MKV for most modern clients, and HEVC (H.265) where the client hardware supports it. Formats that typically require transcoding include WMV, FLV, and any container with an unsupported audio codec (e.g. DTS or FLAC without prior setup).

See [/advanced/hardware-transcoding](/advanced/hardware-transcoding) for hardware-accelerated transcoding and [/reference/config-files](/reference/config-files) for FFmpeg path and codec configuration.

### A library item is unmatched / not found — how do I fix it?

1. Check the file naming convention. Phlix matches movies by `MovieName (Year).ext` and TV by `ShowName S01E01.ext`. See [/libraries/movies](/libraries/movies) and [/libraries/tv-shows](/libraries/tv-shows) for exact patterns.
2. **Fix one title:** use the per-item **Match metadata** action (admin-only, on the media card's ⋯ menu and on the detail page hero). It searches TMDB and applies the result you pick, and for a series it enriches the whole season/episode subtree. This is the most reliable remedy for a single wrong or missing match. See [Fixing a single item's match](/admin/library-management#fixing-a-single-items-match).
3. **Fix a whole library:**

An offset is only useful if the bucket ordering matches the grid's `ORDER BY`.
That holds for `field=name`, where buckets group on `UPPER(LEFT(sort_title,1))` and
the grid orders on `sort_title, name`. It does **not** hold for:

- **`field=rating`** — the grid orders by `rating_score DESC` while the buckets
  group and order on `content_rating`. These are unrelated orderings.
- **`field=date_added`** — the buckets are emitted newest-first and only reversed
  when `order=desc`, so both directions are misaligned.
- **rows with no value** — items with `year <= 0`, `runtime <= 0` or a blank genre
  are dropped from the buckets but still occupy rows in the grid, so every offset
  after them is short by their count.
- **divergent filters** — `minRating` applies to the grid only, and profile tag
  filtering removes rows *after* `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` has been applied.

Treat a jump on those fields as approximate.
:::

tool_input.new_string:
Downloads from S3 if needed, verifies the SHA-256 checksum, extracts the archive, imports `database.sql` via `mysql`, then copies the archived config files over `config/`.

::: danger The restore is NOT atomic and there is no rollback
There is no transaction, no pre-restore snapshot and no compensating action. The
checksum and extraction steps run before anything is written, so a corrupt archive
is rejected harmlessly — but once the `mysql` import has run it cannot be undone,
and a later failure while restoring config files leaves the **database fully
replaced** and `config/` **partially overwritten**.

Partial config state is the normal path, not just the crash path: the restore
copies file-by-file and skips past entries whose parent directory it cannot create
or which fail the containment check, so it can report success having written only a
subset. **Take your own database and `config/` snapshot before restoring.**
:::

**Response `200`:** — the backup id is interpolated into the message.
```json
{ "success": true, "message": "Backup 'abc123' restored successfully" }
```

**Response `500`:** — note `message` carries the failure category and `error` the
detail, not the other way round. On a checksum mismatch:
```json
{ "success": false, "message": "Checksum mismatch", "error": "Expected <a>, got <b>" }
```
`"Restore failed"` appears as the **`error`** value only when an unexpected
exception escapes.

::: warning `enabled` is required, and the schedule is only read at boot
Automatic backups need an explicit truthy `enabled`. The boot-time check reads it as
`empty($backupConfig['enabled'])`, so a `config/backup.php` that **omits** the key
registers no timer at all, whatever `auto_backup_interval_days` says. (A second
reader defaults the same key to `true`, but nothing consumes that value — the
boot-time check is the only live consumer, so the behaviour is unambiguous: no
`enabled`, no automatic backups.) Manual backups from the admin page are unaffected.

Both gates — `enabled` and `auto_backup_interval_days > 0` — are evaluated **once,
at startup**. `PUT /api/v1/admin/backup/schedule` rewrites `config/backup.php` but
does not touch the running process, and the backup manager caches its config for the
process lifetime. **Restart the server for a schedule change to take effect.**
:::

When `enabled` is truthy and `auto_backup_interval_days > 0`, the server registers a scheduled-backup timer at startup. The next scheduled time is returned by `GET /api/v1/admin/backup/schedule`.

### Retention {#retention}

Old backups beyond `retention_count` are deleted after each new backup. Deletion removes **either** the S3 object **or** the local file, depending on the record's `is_s3` flag — never both.

::: warning An uploaded backup leaves its local archive behind forever
"Upload to S3" flips `is_s3` to `true` and replaces the stored `file_path` with the
`s3://` URL **without deleting the local archive**. Retention then only ever deletes
the S3 object for that record, and the on-disk `.tar.gz` path is no longer recorded
anywhere, so no code path can ever clean it up. If you use S3, prune `local_path`
yourself.
:::

## Overview

The pairing protocol establishes a trust relationship between a self-hosted
`phlix-server` instance and a `phlix-hub` instance. Once paired, the hub can:

- Broker authentication so clients can access the server from anywhere
- Provide relay connectivity when direct LAN access is unavailable
- Offer a unified "my servers" dashboard for users with multiple homes

**Since:** 0.16.0

## TL;DR

Phlix provides three layers of household control: **Access Schedules** restrict when users can stream, **Tag Blocking** prevents specific content categories from appearing, and **Stream Limits** cap concurrent streams per user or household.

---

## 1. Access Schedules

### Access Schedules Overview

Access schedules define recurring time windows during which a **profile is blocked** from streaming. Inside a matching window, playback requests are refused with `403`; outside every window, access is allowed.

::: warning Schedules are blackout windows, not permit windows
This is the opposite of how the rest of this section previously described them, and the distinction is load-bearing: a profile with **no** schedules is **unrestricted**, and access is allowed whenever no schedule matches. `AccessScheduleService::isAccessAllowed()` returns true when no active schedule matches the current day and time, so schedules can only ever take access away. Do not rely on "add one allow-window to lock everything else down" — that is not what the implementation does.
:::

### Use Cases

- Bedtime cutoffs for children (e.g., no streaming after 9 PM on school nights)
- Household bandwidth management during peak hours
- Content-free periods (e.g., no streaming during homework hours)

### Configuring Access Schedules

Admins configure schedules in **Admin → Users → [select user] → Access Schedule**.

Each schedule consists of:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Days** | Monday–Sunday checkboxes |
| **Start Time** | When access begins (e.g., 07:00) |
| **End Time** | When access ends (e.g., 22:00) |
| **Timezone** | The timezone the schedule is evaluated in |

## TL;DR

Phlix provides three layers of household control: **Access Schedules** restrict when users can stream, **Tag Blocking** prevents specific content categories from appearing, and **Stream Limits** cap concurrent streams per user or household.

## 1. Access Schedules

### Access Schedules Overview

Access schedules define recurring time windows during which a **profile is blocked** from streaming. Inside a matching window, playback requests are refused with `403`; outside every window, access is allowed.

::: warning Schedules are blackout windows, not permit windows

Do not rely on "add one allow-window to lock everything else down" — that is not what the implementation does.
:::

- Bedtime cutoffs for children (e.g., no streaming after 9 PM on school nights)
- Household bandwidth management during peak hours
- Content-free periods (e.g., no streaming during homework hours)

a separate call to `GET /api/v1/profiles/{id}/active-streams`.

reclaimed on a 60-second heartbeat timeout, not when playback stops, so with the
default cap of 1 a viewer can be locked out of their own next title for a minute.

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/sites/phlix/phlix-docs/docs/hub/library-sharing.md","content":"# Library Sharing

**Since:** 0.19.0

## TL;DR

Library sharing lets you grant a hub user access to one of your libraries by email — no link required. You choose the library, set a permission level, and optionally add an expiry. The collaborator sees the shared library under **"Shared with me"** immediately after you share it.

---

## The Shares Page

Both "libraries I've shared" and "shared with me" live together on the single
**Shares** page (`/app/shares`), reached from the hub's top navigation. (The
legacy `/manage-shares` and `/shared-with-me` pages still resolve, but `/app/shares`
is the current entry point.)

### Libraries I've Shared

The **Shares** page lists every library share you have created, one row per share:

```
┌─ Library    Shared With    Permission   Shared On   Actions ────────┐
│ Movies ★   alice@example.com  Read only   2026-05-29  [Edit] [Revoke]│
│ TV Shows   bob@example.com    Read/Write  2026-05-29  [Edit] [Revoke]│
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### Reading a share row

Each row shows:

- **Library** — the library being shared.
- **Shared With** — the collaborator's email address.
- **Permission** — `Read` or `Read/Write`. Shown as a coloured badge.
- **Shared On** — the date the share was created.
- **Actions** — **Edit** lets you change the permission inline. **Revoke** deletes the share immediately.

### Shared With Me

The same **Shares** page also lists every library another hub user has shared with you, one card per library:

```
┌─ Library ──────────────────────────────┐
│ Movies ★                               │
│ Shared by: Alice (alice@example.com)   │
│ Server: My Server                     │
│ Permission: Read only                  │
│                         [Browse Library]│
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```\

{"stdout":"# Share Libraries with Friends and Family

## TL;DR

Hub sharing lets you grant access to your media library to friends and family through the hub. Open the **Shares** page (`/app/shares`) → choose what to share → invite by email or link. Recipients see your server under **"Shared with me"** on the same **Shares** page in their hub account without needing to install anything or be on the same network. Permissions are configurable from view-only to full playback with optional download access.

---

## 1. How Hub Sharing Works

The sharing model is simple:

- **You** (library owner) grant access from the **Shares** page (`/app/shares`)
- **Your friend** receives an invite by email or a shareable link
- **Your friend** logs into the hub and sees your server under **"Shared with me"** on the **Shares** page
- **You** retain full control — revoke or change permissions at any time

### Three sharing scopes

| Scope | What the recipient sees |
|---|---|
| Entire library | All items in the selected library |
| Specific folders | Only the folders you chose (e.g., `Movies/Classics`) |
| Specific media items | Only the individual items you selected |

### Three permission levels

| Permission | Browse | Play | Cast / DLNA | Download |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **View only** | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **View + Playback** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **View + Playback + Download** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

> **Note:** DLNA casting requires the `View + Playback + Download` permission — the download component enables the stream to be redirected to a DLNA renderer.

---

1. Log into the hub at `https://hub.phlix.app` (or your self-hosted hub URL)
2. Open the **Shares** page (`/app/shares`) from the top navigation
3. Click **Share Library**
4. Choose what to share (entire library, specific folders, or specific items)
5. Select the permission level: **View only** / **View + Playback** / **View + Playback + Do

grep "share_invite_accepted" .logs/hub-audit.log | tail -10
# The log shows the invited email vs. the accepting account email
```

---
"""

Earlier revisions of this page said the invite "is tied to the exact email address

**whoever redeems it**, using their own account email. A link is bounded only by its
**max uses** and its **expiry** — not by identity.

Anyone who obtains the URL, by forwarding or interception, can redeem it. Send links
over a channel you trust, set a low max-use count, and keep the expiry short.
:::

**Symptom:** Someone other than the intended recipient now has access.

**Fix:** Revoke the share on `/app/shares`, and delete or expire the invite link so
it cannot be redeemed again.

---
"""

# On the server, check library status via the API:

```

**Fix:** Library sharing requires the library scan to be complete. If a scan is still in progress, wait for it to finish. If no scan is running, trigger one manually. The friend should refresh the hub page after the scan completes and verify the library contents.

- **`docs/hub/share-with-friends.md`** claimed an invite link "is tied to the exact
  email address it was sent to". The opposite is true: the share is created for

  it would forward a link believing it was safe. Now documented as a bearer token.

  callers in either class and is pinned only by its own unit tests. Both hub pages
  said permissions were "configurable from view-only to full playback".

  request". Direct play is served **before the router**, so no access-schedule check
  applies to it: a profile inside a blackout window can still direct-play. An
